title: Towards a Sharp Analysis of Offline Policy Learning for $f$-Divergence-Regularized Contextual Bandits
claim: Empirical error decays at the predicted rate as sample size grows, matching theory across regularizers and settings.
layout: 3 panels left-to-right, log-log plots with fitted-rate legends
description: Three side-by-side log-log scatter plots with dashed linear fits and light grid lines. The left panel, titled for KL sub-optimality, shows two decreasing lines, purple x markers and brown plus markers, for two reference policies. Legends give fitted slopes of about -0.98 and -0.97. The middle panel shows f-divergence (chi-squared) sub-optimality as blue circles and orange squares. They fall along nearly parallel lines with fitted rates of -0.98 and -0.99. The right panel shows red diamonds hovering around a flat horizontal level when n times alpha is held fixed. This indicates sub-optimality scales inversely with the regularization weight. Axes are powers of two in n against expected sub-optimality. Subcaptions (a) and (b) sit below. The eye goes first to the steep diagonal lines on the left.
caption: The empirical relation between log2 n and log2 SubOpt. The fitted rate means the slope of log2 n ∼log2 SubOpt estimated via linear regression. Here n is the sample size. Every point is the average over 100 independent trials.
abstract: Many offline reinforcement learning algorithms are underpinned by $f$-divergence regularization, but their sample complexity *defined with respect to regularized objectives* still lacks tight analyses, especially in terms of concrete data coverage conditions. In this paper, we study the exact concentrability requirements to achieve the $\tildeÎ(Îµ^{-1})$ sample complexity for offline $f$-divergence-regularized contextual bandits. For reverse Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence, arguably the most commonly used one, we achieve an $\tilde{O}(Îµ^{-1})$ sample complexity under single-policy concentrability for the first time via a novel pessimism-based analysis, surpassing existing $\tilde{O}(Îµ^{-1})$ bound under all-policy concentrability and $\tilde{O}(Îµ^{-2})$ bound under single-policy concentrability. We also propose a near-matching lower bound, demonstrating that a multiplicative dependency on single-policy concentrability is necessary to maximally exploit the curvature property of reverse KL. Moreover, for $f$-divergences with strongly convex $f$, to which reverse KL *does not* belong, we show that the sharp sample complexity $\tildeÎ(Îµ^{-1})$ is achievable even without pessimistic estimation or single-policy concentrability. We further corroborate our theoretical insights with numerical experiments and extend our analysis to contextual dueling bandits. We believe these results take a significant step towards a comprehensive understanding of objectives with $f$-divergence regularization.
